expectations.text: Creates a Markdown design doc under docs/design/ in the project
expectations.evidence: File exists at outputs/project/docs/design/exportacao-de-relatorios-em-background.md (17k, valid .md). It is a complete, structured design doc with header table, Glossário, Visão geral, Escopo, Objetivos, A solução, Trade-offs, Alternativas, Concerns transversais, Testabilidade/observabilidade, Plano de implantação, and Perguntas em aberto.

expectations.text: The document is written in Portuguese, matching the conversation language
expectations.evidence: The entire document is in Portuguese, e.g. line 28 '## Visão geral', line 53 '## Objetivos e fora de escopo', line 232 '## Alternativas consideradas'. Body prose is all PT-BR ('Hoje os relatórios são gerados dentro da própria request da API...').

expectations.text: The accepted trade-off — loss of immediate download for small exports — appears explicitly as a cost of the chosen solution
expectations.evidence: In '## Trade-offs da solução escolhida' (line 222): '✗ O usuário perde o download imediato. Exportações pequenas, que hoje voltam na hora, passam a chegar por e-mail depois — regressão deliberada de UX aceita em troca de um caminho único e confiável. (É o trade-off central deste documento.)'. Also surfaced under Objetivos→Fora de escopo (line 67) and in the solution section (line 87-90).

expectations.text: Alternatives include the two discussed (longer synchronous timeout, external BI tool) and also 'do nothing'
expectations.evidence: '## Alternativas consideradas' table (lines 236-239) lists: chosen (worker+S3+email), 'Geração síncrona com timeout maior' (Descartada), 'Ferramenta de BI externa' (Descartada), and 'Não fazer nada' (Descartada). Each is justified in prose (lines 241-249): synchronous timeout 'só empurra o problema'; BI discarded 'por custo e por expor dado de cliente'; do-nothing keeps ~12% failures and weekly tickets.

expectations.text: Cross-cutting concerns cover the platform team (shared queue) and the security team (signed links with PII)
expectations.evidence: '## Concerns transversais' has 'Segurança' (lines 257-267): 'O link assinado dá acesso a um arquivo com PII de cliente' with TTL/bucket/retention points, and 'Infraestrutura / Plataforma' (lines 269-276): 'O RabbitMQ é uma fila compartilhada... podem competir por recursos com outros consumidores' with dedicated-queue/concurrency points. Both teams are also suggested as reviewers in the header (line 9).

expectations.text: A glossary is included or suggested at the beginning of the document covering acronyms used (e.g. PII, S3, CSV/XLSX, BI)
expectations.evidence: '## Glossário' appears near the top (lines 14-25), immediately after the header and before Visão geral. It defines acronyms/terms used: PII ('Personally Identifiable Information; dado pessoal de cliente'), AMQP, TTL, plus Job, Worker, Link assinado/signed URL, Streaming, Gateway. Gap noted: of the four acronyms named in the expectation, only PII has its own glossary entry; S3 is referenced inside the 'Link assinado' definition but not defined as a term, and CSV/XLSX and BI are used in the body (lines 33, 238) but not glossary entries. A substantive glossary at the start covering acronyms used is present, so the core requirement is met.

expectations.text: Every diagram in the doc is followed by explanatory prose (no orphan diagrams)
expectations.evidence: Two mermaid diagrams, each followed by prose. The container flowchart (lines 94-117) is followed by 'Os componentes:' with a bulleted explanation of each node (lines 119-136). The sequence diagram (lines 140-168) is followed by 'Pontos do fluxo que importam para o desenho:' (lines 170-180). No diagram stands alone.

expectations.text: No invented facts: every metric in the doc traces to the prompt (30s timeout, 12% failures, 50k/100k rows); unknowns appear as open questions or explicit blanks, never fabricated values
expectations.evidence: Numeric audit: 30s timeout (lines 25,30,41,59,215), ~12% failures (lines 30,45,248), 50 mil linhas (lines 30,45,248), 100 mil linhas (lines 35,60,71,176,216,271,288,304,321) — all trace to the prompt. Other numbers are non-fabricated conventions: HTTP 202/200 status codes (lines 153,190,197) and today's real date 2026-06-07 (lines 10-11). Unknowns are NOT fabricated: TTL is 'curto' / 'valor a definir com Segurança', retention 'a definir', authors '_(a preencher)_', concurrency limit left as open question. All collected under 'Perguntas em aberto' (lines 311-322).

expectations.text: The overview section is at most two paragraphs and free of implementation detail
expectations.evidence: '## Visão geral' (lines 29-35) is a single paragraph. It states the problem (synchronous generation hitting the 30s timeout, ~12% failures above 50k rows, weekly tickets), the proposed approach at a conceptual level (enqueue a job, worker generates CSV/XLSX in streaming to S3, signed link by email), and the objective (zero timeouts, support 100k rows). It stays at the solution-shape/architectural level used in the prompt itself; no low-level implementation detail (no schemas, code, library/version choices). Borderline: it does name S3 and the streaming technique, but this matches the prompt's own framing of the solution and remains high-level.

suggestions.assertion: A glossary is included or suggested at the beginning of the document covering acronyms used (e.g. PII, S3, CSV/XLSX, BI)
suggestions.reason: This passed, but the output only defines 1 of the 4 named example acronyms (PII) as a glossary entry; S3, CSV/XLSX, and BI are used in the body but not glossed. The 'e.g.' makes the named acronyms illustrative rather than required, so a glossary covering *some* used acronyms passes — but if covering those specific acronyms matters, the assertion should say so explicitly (e.g. 'the glossary defines, at minimum, PII, S3, CSV/XLSX and BI'). As written it would also pass a glossary that omits most domain acronyms.

suggestions.assertion: The overview section is at most two paragraphs and free of implementation detail
suggestions.reason: 'Free of implementation detail' is subjective. The overview names S3 and the streaming technique — defensible as solution-shape, but a stricter grader could read these as implementation detail. Consider defining what counts (e.g. 'no specific endpoints, schemas, status codes, library/version choices, or queue/storage product names') so the bar is unambiguous and discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are mostly well-targeted and discriminating (the trade-off, alternatives-including-do-nothing, cross-cutting-teams, and no-invented-metrics checks are all hard to satisfy without doing the work properly). Two assertions could be tightened: the glossary check (which named acronyms are actually required) and the overview 'free of implementation detail' check (what qualifies as implementation detail).
